mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: lower rates compress discount rates and boost equity valuations, leading to positive returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is above 3.0%, the market anticipates prolonged monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the market prices in higher risk premiums and reduced growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The level of housing starts (HOUST) is positively related to S&P 500 forward returns: higher housing activity signals a strong economy and positive returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST is above 1100, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0%, it signals a weakening labor market and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceed 145000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.5%, it signals a strong labor market that supports economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 145000 AND UNRATE < 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (the 2017 base), it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
